new_symbol_range_suggestions.chi: 0 <= chi <= 2 as an independently sampled condition; values near 0 suppress the extended-harmonic channel, values near 1 recover comparable channel weighting

derivation_notes: The parent combines the two lattice harmonics into one common screened correction, implicitly assuming identical environmental screening for both effective force channels. The successor resolves those channels before the nonlinear square-root map, so the environment can redistribute curvature between the sin(kappa/2)**2 and sin(kappa)**2 contributions through separate rational saturation of each harmonic branch.
change_summary: Promoted chi from a fixed parameter to a sampled condition and changed the law so the fundamental and extended reciprocal-space harmonics are screened separately. This creates a real eta-chi interaction in the scored Omega surface, visible as condition-dependent mid-zone reshaping even when the long-wavelength acoustic behavior stays similar.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The additional reciprocal-space harmonic weighted by chi responds to the environment with the same effective screening law as the fundamental nonlocal harmonic contribution.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Different effective further-neighbor force channels can have different screening lengths, so the environment changes the projected Fourier weights of distinct lattice harmonics rather than only scaling one fixed mixture.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: At the reference condition chi = 1 and when the two channels are effectively indistinguishable in the weak-screening limit zeta*eta*(sin(kappa/2)**2 + sin(kappa)**2) << 1, the successor approaches the parent form with a common harmonic mixture.

response_change.parent_relation: The environment control eta rescales a single screened nonlocal correction built from one common rational saturation of sin(kappa/2)^2 + chi*sin(kappa)^2, so all eta-dependent shape changes are tied to one fixed mixture set by chi.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption that the two reciprocal-space harmonics experience the environment identically, so eta changes the relative weight of the sin(kappa/2)^2 and sin(kappa)^2 contributions through distinct screening of short- and longer-range effective couplings.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed chi, increasing eta changes not only the overall curvature enhancement but also the kappa-location and sharpness of mid-zone flattening/steepening; a single parent parameter set cannot match two conditions where the small-k slope enhancement is similar but the mid-zone shape differs.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Visible for moderate nonlocal correction eta not asymptotically small and for wavevectors away from the strict acoustic limit, especially intermediate zone fractions where both sin(kappa/2)^2 and sin(kappa)^2 are appreciable; if eta is tiny or kappa is near 0 or the zone edge only, the contrast is weak.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, eta-dependent curvature changes already appear; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to condition-dependent redistribution between low-k and mid-zone dispersion shape rather than a uniform family controlled by one fixed harmonic mixture.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the two harmonic channels share the same environment response, i.e. in the limit of identical screening/saturation for both contributions or when the extra distinction parameter tends to the value enforcing a common denominator/weighting.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: With chi fixed, the parent forces one environment-independent harmonic mixture across all conditions. Releasing chi as a sampled condition allows physically admissible environment-dependent redistribution between reciprocal-space harmonics without adding a new mechanism outside the existing nonlocal harmonic picture.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: channel-specific screening of distinct reciprocal-space harmonic contributions from effective further-neighbor couplings
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Different effective further-neighbor force channels generally have different spatial decay or screening lengths, so the environment can alter the projected Fourier weights of distinct lattice harmonics rather than merely scaling one fixed mixture.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The refinement is harder than coefficient retuning because the two harmonic diagnostics are separately combined with eta inside distinct rational screening factors before being recombined under the outer square root. That nested interaction lets eta reshape the harmonic balance across kappa, rather than only amplifying a fixed pre-mixed spectrum.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: A single screened mixture governs both reciprocal-space harmonics, with chi fixed across conditions.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The extended-harmonic channel weight chi is condition-dependent and the two reciprocal-space harmonics are screened separately by the environment before entering the final nonlinear response.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: When the distinction between channel screenings becomes negligible, especially in the weak-screening limit where both denominators are close to 1, the child reduces to the parent's common-mixture behavior.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Holding zeta fixed while varying eta and the promoted condition chi, one can find cases with comparable low-k acoustic slope but different intermediate-k curvature and shoulder strength because the full-zone harmonic saturates differently from the half-zone harmonic. The parent only produces eta-dependent deformations along one fixed harmonic-mixture family, so it cannot realize that redistributed mid-zone shape with one shared parameter set.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting the parent's existing parameters cannot absorb this across conditions because its eta dependence enters only through one shared rational function of sin(kappa/2)**2 + chi*sin(kappa)**2. Once that common mixture is fixed, matching the low-k enhancement also fixes how the mid-zone contribution saturates. The child breaks that structural tying by assigning separate screened branches to the two harmonics, so one shared parent parameter set cannot reproduce condition-dependent redistribution between them.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Visible for moderate nonlocal correction eta not asymptotically small and for wavevectors away from the strict acoustic limit, especially intermediate zone fractions where both sin(kappa/2)^2 and sin(kappa)^2 are appreciable; if eta is tiny or kappa is near 0 or the zone edge only, the contrast is weak.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, eta-dependent curvature changes already appear; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to condition-dependent redistribution between low-k and mid-zone dispersion shape rather than a uniform family controlled by one fixed harmonic mixture.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the two harmonic channels share the same environment response, i.e. in the limit of identical screening/saturation for both contributions or when the extra distinction parameter tends to the value enforcing a common denominator/weighting.
evolution_plan.promotion_reason: With chi fixed, the parent forces one environment-independent harmonic mixture across all conditions. Releasing chi as a sampled condition allows physically admissible environment-dependent redistribution between reciprocal-space harmonics without adding a new mechanism outside the existing nonlocal harmonic picture.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes that all environment dependence enters through one shared screened combination of the two lattice harmonics, so the relative importance of the extended-harmonic component is fixed across conditions.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The additional reciprocal-space harmonic weighted by chi responds to the environment with the same effective screening law as the fundamental nonlocal harmonic contribution.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Different effective further-neighbor force channels generally have different spatial decay or screening lengths, so the environment can alter the projected Fourier weights of distinct lattice harmonics rather than merely scaling one fixed mixture.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: Omega is |sin(kappa/2)| times a square-root correction whose eta dependence is carried by a single rational function of a fixed harmonic combination sin(kappa/2)^2 + chi*sin(kappa)^2. Thus, once chi is fixed, varying eta can only strengthen or saturate one predetermined shape family. Child change: allow the relative contribution of the higher harmonic to vary with condition, representing differential screening of coupling channels with different spatial range. Distinguishing condition: vary eta and the promoted condition chi across admissible environments while holding the lattice spacing, nearest-neighbor reference stiffness, and zeta fixed; then compare two cases with similar low-k acoustic behavior but different intermediate-k curvature or shoulder strength. The parent with one shared parameter set cannot reproduce this because its eta dependence is separable through one fixed harmonic mixture, so matching the low-k trend also locks the mid-zone redistribution. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation, because the scored Omega(kappa,eta,chi) surface itself gains a condition-dependent interaction between eta and harmonic content. Scientifically admissible activation requires non-negligible effective nonlocal coupling and measurements spanning intermediate kappa; if only very small kappa are observed, both parent and child collapse toward the same acoustic limit and the refinement is weak.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Combine declared quantities before applying a nonlinear map, such as relative speed followed by quadratic drag.

scenario_text: Consider the acoustic vibrational branch of a one-dimensional monatomic crystal measured across its first reciprocal-space zone. The atoms interact through identical harmonic nearest-neighbor bonds, so collective lattice vibrations determine the mode frequency. Predict the normalized phonon frequency from the dimensionless wavevector while the lattice spacing and bond stiffness remain fixed. The response must capture both the long-wavelength acoustic limit and the turnover imposed by lattice periodicity.
